questions.q: According to this lesson, what should you check first when a query or pipeline breaks?
options: The Snowflake status page only
Re-run the exact same query immediately with no investigation
Query History — every query run, filterable by status, user, warehouse, and time
Nothing — Snowflake provides no way to see past queries
questions.explain: Query History (Snowsight's Activity tab) is the first stop — it shows every run and lets you filter straight to the failed one.

questions.q: What does the Query Profile tab show for a selected query?
options: A list of unrelated queries from other users
A step-by-step breakdown of its execution plan, including the most expensive steps and row counts
Only the raw SQL text with no execution detail
The warehouse's billing invoice
questions.explain: Query Profile breaks a single query's run into steps, showing timing, row counts, and which step cost the most — Snowflake's equivalent of an execution plan, always available after the fact.

questions.q: What is the key difference between INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY() and SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY?
options: ACCOUNT_USAGE only works for Snowpipe loads
INFORMATION_SCHEMA requires ACCOUNTADMIN privileges and ACCOUNT_USAGE does not
INFORMATION_SCHEMA covers roughly the last 7 days with no lag; ACCOUNT_USAGE covers up to a year, account-wide, with up to ~45 minutes of lag
They return completely unrelated data with no overlap
questions.explain: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY() is fast and current but short-retention; ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY holds much longer history account-wide but lags real time by up to about 45 minutes.

questions.q: What question does COPY_HISTORY answer that plain Query History does not directly answer?
options: Which role owns a given database
How much a warehouse costs per hour
Whether a specific file actually loaded into a specific table, and why it failed if it didn't
What the current session's timezone is set to
questions.explain: COPY_HISTORY tracks individual file load status (LOADED, load failures, error messages) for both manual COPY INTO runs and Snowpipe loads — a narrower, file-level question than general query success/failure.

questions.q: COPY_HISTORY is the same load-tracking mechanism behind which two loading methods covered earlier in this course?
options: Manual COPY INTO statements and Snowpipe's continuous ingestion
Streams and Tasks
SCD Type 1 and SCD Type 2 updates
Power BI DirectQuery and Import mode
questions.explain: COPY_HISTORY tracks file-level load status for both COPY INTO (Chapter 3) and Snowpipe (Chapter 4) — the same history view covers both loading paths.
